source_row.rationale: The Parkland formula for burn fluid resuscitation typically directs that half of the calculated total 24-hour fluid volume be administered in the first 8 hours from the time of injury (not from the time of hospital arrival, which is an important distinction if there was a delay in reaching care), with the remaining half administered over the following 16 hours, reflecting the pattern of fluid shifts and capillary leak that occurs after a major burn.
